intro: Unit III: Writing Skills for TNPSC Group 2/2A Prelims focuses on essential language and writing competencies. This unit covers formal and informal letter writing, sentence arrangement, and critical reading skills like making queries and inferences.

sections.heading: Letter Writing
points: Formal letters are written to official authorities and require a formal tone, specific address, and a clear subject line.
Informal letters are written to friends or family, allowing a personal, conversational, and relaxed tone.
Always include the date, address, salutation, body, complimentary close, and signature in the correct format.
The purpose of the letter must be clearly stated in the opening paragraph to ensure effective communication.

sections.heading: Jumbled Sentences
points: Read all the given sentences carefully to understand the main idea and the overall context of the paragraph.
Look for connecting words, pronouns, or transitional phrases that link two sentences together.
Arrange the sentences logically, typically starting with an introductory sentence and moving to supporting details.

sections.heading: Making Queries & Inferences
points: Making queries involves identifying what information is missing, unclear, or requires further explanation in a given text.
Inferences are logical conclusions drawn by connecting clues provided in the text with your own general knowledge.
Practice identifying the underlying meaning or unstated assumptions of the author to master inference questions.

sections.heading: Fill in the Blanks & Substitutions
points: For fill-in-the-blanks, select the word that best fits the grammatical structure and the semantic context of the sentence.
Check for subject-verb agreement, tense consistency, and correct prepositions when choosing the right word.
In substitution questions, replace the highlighted word with the most appropriate synonym without changing the sentence's core meaning.

exam_tips: Practice previous years' question papers to understand the exact pattern and difficulty level of TNPSC Group 2 Prelims.
Manage your time strictly; if a question is too difficult, mark it and move on to secure easy marks first.
Read the entire question carefully before selecting an option to avoid common grammatical traps.
